subject.title: feat: provider fallback by failure class — quarantine auth-broken providers

question: Should ordinary provider auth failures become a default hard-quarantine signal, and what confirmation/status contract should distinguish transient 401s from broken auth profiles?
rationale: The remaining behavior changes provider selection, operator-visible status, and upgrade semantics for existing auth setups, so automation should not choose the default quarantine policy alone.

options.title: Default confirmed-auth quarantine
options.body: Quarantine a provider/profile only after a maintainer-defined repeated failure or same-key confirmation threshold, then expose redacted incident health through status and doctor surfaces.

options.title: Keep opt-in skip behavior
options.body: Leave default runtime retries unchanged, document the existing opt-in skip cache and doctor/status workflows, and close only the narrower log-spam and relogin gaps already fixed elsewhere.

options.title: Defer to live provider repro
options.body: Wait for a redacted live reproduction of the Anthropic/Codex 401 restart cases before changing default provider selection behavior.

recommendation.title: Default confirmed-auth quarantine
recommendation.body: Quarantine a provider/profile only after a maintainer-defined repeated failure or same-key confirmation threshold, then expose redacted incident health through status and doctor surfaces.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining decision is cross-cutting provider/auth runtime policy and status behavior, and steipete has the strongest recent area-maintainer signal in the current history available for these central paths.
